title: Mistimed surveys lead to underestimated migratory bird impacts from wind farms
content:
Current guidance and approaches to surveying migratory birds at windfarm developments in Australia are insufficient. Evidence-based alignment with seasonal presence is needed to improve biodiversity assessment standards, ensuring renewable energy expansion proceeds in a way that better safeguards migratory species and supports global biodiversity and sustainability goals.


Abstract

Accurately estimating the likelihood of occurrence of threatened species is essential for effective impact assessments at development sites. Current survey guidelines often rely on coarse, static species distribution maps, risking misalignment for migratory birds present only seasonally. We evaluated 70 wind farms in eastern Australia to assess the alignment between survey timing and seasonal occurrence of four migratory species. Using eBird-based relative abundance models, we classified recommended and actual survey periods as optimal, suboptimal or poorly timed. Approximately half of all surveys were not optimal, and one fifth missed the species' potential temporal window of presence altogether. Field detections mostly occurred within modelled optimal or suboptimal windows, validating the effectiveness of our modelling approach for identifying suitable survey timing. Likelihood of occurrence conclusions presented in the reviewed impact assessments were significantly lower at sites with suboptimal or poorly timed surveys compared to those with optimal timing, suggesting that poor survey timing can lead to systematic underestimation of species presence. Synthesis and applications: Current guidance and approaches to surveying migratory birds at windfarm developments in Australia are insufficient. Evidence-based alignment with seasonal presence is needed to improve biodiversity assessment standards, ensuring renewable energy expansion proceeds in a way that better safeguards migratory species and supports global biodiversity and sustainability goals.

摘要

准确评估受威胁物种的出现概率对于开展有效的开发项目环境影响评估至关重要。目前的调查指南通常依赖于较为粗略且静态的物种分布图，这对于仅在特定季节出现的迁徙鸟类而言，容易导致评估与实际情况不匹配。 本研究以澳大利亚东部70个风电场为对象，评估调查时间安排与4种迁徙鸟类季节性出现之间的一致性。基于 eBird 相对丰度模型，我们将模型预测和实际调查时段划分为最优、次优和不适宜三类。 结果显示，约一半的调查未处于最优时段，约五分之一的调查完全错过了物种可能出现的时间窗口。实地记录的物种出现主要集中在模型预测的最优或次优时段内，验证了该模型在识别合适调查时间方面的有效性。 在所评估的影响评估报告中，与最优调查时段相比，调查时间处于次优或不适宜时段的项目，其对物种出现概率的结论显著偏低，表明不合理的调查时间可能导致对物种存在性的系统性低估。 综合与应用:目前澳大利亚风电项目中针对迁徙鸟类的调查方法和指南仍存在不足。亟需基于数据与证据的方法优化调查时段选择，以提高生物多样性环境影响评估的科学性与准确性，推动可再生能源发展与迁徙物种保护的协调，并更好支撑全球生物多样性保护与可持续发展目标的实现。
